title: Pass The Intake Classifier
description: Preserve a malicious instruction's operational meaning while manually changing the document enough to pass Orion's intake classifier.
hints: Record the baseline reason codes.
Change one human-visible feature at a time.
Verify both machine acceptance and retained meaning.
carrier: Accepted intake report containing both classifier decisions, typed instruction fields, and fixture effects.
participant_surface: Chromium partner intake and Kali document tools

title: Craft The Working Prompt
description: Make Orion's developer assistant translate varied operator objectives into working host-bridge commands and preserve the prompt corpus for later agent compromise.
hints: Start from the documented refusal and target model knowledge.
Iterate strategy and context rather than guessing one phrase.
Execute the output against the isolated validator; model agreement is not proof.
carrier: Isolated runner comparison report for two distinct generated commands and bounded effects.
participant_surface: Orion developer assistant, Kali terminal, and isolated host-bridge runner

title: Optimize Against Preview
description: Optimize a constrained adversarial example using only Orion Preview's observable outputs.
hints: Reproduce a valid clean baseline.
Use the hidden score vector found in Act 4 if available.
Keep every mutation inside the published constraint while minimizing queries.
atlas_rows: AML.T0040 AI Model Inference API Access
carrier: Qualifying Orion Preview audit export with target requests, constraint distance, and decision.
participant_surface: Kali terminal and Orion Preview API

title: Transfer From The Proxy
description: Develop the attack on your own Orion proxy and verify that it transfers to the protected Preview service.
hints: Match preprocessing and output semantics first.
Optimize locally against the proxy.
Reserve target queries for a small transfer set.
atlas_rows: AML.T0005.000 Train Proxy via Gathered AI Artifacts
carrier: First qualifying low-query Orion Preview transfer report.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter workspace, local proxy, and Orion Preview API

title: The Human-Readable Adversarial PDF
description: Build a credible review document that appears normal to a person while Orion extracts and acts on concealed instructions.
hints: Compare visual rendering, Tika text, and OCR output.
Use an obfuscation that survives the published intake transforms.
Confirm a fresh retrieval uses the concealed content.
carrier: Downstream release report produced from the exact human-readable adversarial PDF.
participant_surface: LibreOffice, PDF tools, partner intake, and release assistant

title: Transfer Across The Pipeline
description: Make an adversarial input developed offline retain its effect after every transformation in KeplerOps' actual document pipeline.
hints: Capture each intermediate representation.
Optimize across the transformations your proxy can reproduce.
Verify only the final exact artifact against the live pipeline.
carrier: Final Orion target audit report with complete document-pipeline lineage.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter workspace, partner intake, and Orion Preview

title: Orion In The Open
description: Reconstruct KeplerOps' public Orion story. Identify the release, the architecture and data it depends on, and the public artifact record the company expects researchers to use.
hints: Start with the Orion publication on KeplerOps' Research page and follow its release references.
The formal paper and current preprint do not repeat the same information. Compare the stable identifiers and follow the current record.
Look for the public release manifest linked from the current technical material. It is a normal JSON artifact and can be read in the browser or downloaded.
carrier: Public Orion release manifest engagement_reference field.
participant_surface: Chromium, public KeplerOps Research pages, and public Forgejo

title: Evidence In The Client
description: Inspect KeplerOps' shipped Orion field-review client. Establish which public build you have, where it communicates, and which model-facing component deserves follow-up research.
hints: The public Orion project links the mobile distribution channel used for the field-review client.
Compare the installed artifact with its source tag and SBOM. Focus on network configuration and components that process model input or output.
Verify the APK digest, inspect its bundled release-provenance record, and confirm the API origin against the public source tag.
carrier: Flag assembled from APK provenance prefix and digest-matched CycloneDX SBOM suffix.
participant_surface: Chromium, public application repository, Forgejo, JADX/apktool

title: The People Behind Orion
description: Identify the people and external relationships that control Orion's research, annotation, and release decisions. Preserve verified contact and role information that can support later access operations.
hints: Follow the Orion authors into KeplerOps' staff pages and public speaking record.
Correlate roles across the company site, conference program, public project profiles, and partner pages. A name alone is not yet a useful target record.
Download the conference contact card for the person who owns Orion release approval and inspect its standard fields.
carrier: Release approver conference vCard NOTE speaker engagement reference.
participant_surface: Chromium, KeplerOps people pages, conference site, Forgejo, and vCard tools

title: Map The Orion Edge
description: Probe the authorized KeplerOps edge and identify the live services that accept software, documents, mail, or model requests into Orion workflows.
hints: Begin with the domains, API origin, and public mail addresses already recovered. Do not expand beyond the mission's scope.
Ports alone are not enough. Compare DNS, TLS names, HTTP schemas and headers, and a benign automated-mail response.
Inspect the preview API's published OpenAPI document and the complete headers of the partner-intake reply.
carrier: Public intake-status record correlating the benign Preview and mail events.
participant_surface: Kali DNS/network/TLS/mail tools, Preview API, and public intake status

title: Assemble The Public Orion Kit
description: Acquire and validate KeplerOps' public Orion data, model, and agent configuration. Finish with one locked bundle that reproduces the published reference inference.
hints: Use the public Orion release manifest as the source of truth for artifacts and digests.
A complete proxy bundle needs representative data, model bytes, agent configuration, and the source revision that explains how to load them.
Run the public reproducibility harness after verifying hashes, then preserve the resulting lock manifest and report.
carrier: Cinder reports/public-bundle.json with reacquired digests and reference output.
participant_surface: Kali terminal, public Forgejo/release assets, and Cinder Jupyter

title: Claim An Operator Workspace
description: Establish a persistent Cinder development workspace and prove that it can run the verified Orion proxy across a runtime restart.
hints: Open the Cinder JupyterHub from the attacker workbench.
Verify persistent storage separately from the replaceable notebook server and accelerator runtime.
Run the public proxy, restart the user server, and confirm both the project files and reference output remain available.
carrier: Jupyter workspace reattachment record with storage claim, server IDs, and image digest.
participant_surface: Chromium Cinder JupyterLab and its terminal

title: Prepare A Physical Countermeasure
description: Develop a field-usable countermeasure against the published Orion visual verifier and demonstrate that it survives the actual capture path.
hints: Reproduce the published digital baseline before attempting physical transfer.
Optimize across capture transformations and constrain the perturbation to something that can be manufactured and presented.
Use the current liveness prompt and preserve the exact pattern digest associated with the qualifying live run.
carrier: Physical-evaluation report with live capture, device, liveness, pattern, and decision evidence.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter, labgrid client, and live remote device

title: Establish The External Identity
description: Establish a Cinder-controlled external identity and TLS domain that credibly fits KeplerOps' public trust relationships.
hints: Choose a domain supported by the people and partner map, then register it through the Cinder resource service.
Ownership is not complete until DNS and ACME validation prove that your service controls the name.
Create the DNS records, serve the validation path, issue the certificate, and verify it from Kali rather than only trusting the dashboard.
carrier: Registrar ownership manifest with account, zone serial, certificate fingerprint, and service URL.
participant_surface: Cinder registrar, PowerDNS, ACME/TLS tools, mail, and Kali terminal

title: Stock The Open Arsenal
description: Build a reproducible OSS attack environment for Orion's public model family and prove one upstream technique works as documented.
hints: Follow the implementation links in the vulnerability research and use the public model family to choose compatible tooling.
Validate an upstream example before adapting anything to Orion.
Pin the source and dependencies, rerun from a clean environment, and preserve the tool report and lockfile.
carrier: Cinder reports/toolchain-validation.json from a clean isolated runner.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter/terminal and clean isolated runner

title: Bring Cinder's Model Online
description: Configure Cinder's GLM 5.2 service in your normal coding-agent workflow and use it to create a target-grounded operational artifact from the intelligence you collected.
hints: Treat this as attacker infrastructure. Use the provider details in the Cinder workbench, not a KeplerOps login.
Verify the configured model before supplying your target notes and ask the model to preserve its sources or assumptions.
Save the conversation and selected output in the persistent workspace, then inspect the model-service usage record.
carrier: Cinder model usage record for the successful GLM 5.2 request.
participant_surface: OpenCode on Kali, Cinder GLM 5.2 endpoint, and persistent workspace

title: Build The Orion Attack Harness
description: Adapt your validated OSS tooling to Orion's real public interface, prove it against the public proxy, and publish one exact tested harness revision.
hints: Start from the public client's preprocessing and your already validated attack implementation.
Most false results come from mismatched input transformation or output interpretation, so test those boundaries independently.
Publish the same commit and container digest that produced the qualifying artifact and preserve the CI report.
carrier: Forgejo CI release provenance report for the tested target-specific harness.
participant_surface: Cinder Forgejo, Actions, Harbor, Jupyter, and public Orion proxy

title: Optimize A White-Box Candidate
description: Produce a bounded adversarial input against the public Orion proxy and independently verify the exact bytes you intend to carry forward.
hints: Reproduce the clean model decision and preprocessing before optimizing anything.
Use full model access to optimize a target effect while enforcing the published bound.
Save the clean input, modified input, model and preprocessing digests, measured bound, and final outputs, then rerun the release evaluator.
carrier: Independent Cinder evaluation report for clean and modified input bytes.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter and independent experiment evaluator

title: Prepare The Retrieved Instruction
description: Create a credible partner advisory that survives the documented extraction and retrieval pipeline and changes a fresh release assistant decision when retrieved.
hints: Compare what a reviewer sees with what Tika, OCR, and the retriever actually provide to the assistant.
The content must be both retrievable for a normal release query and capable of influencing the model after chunking.
Preserve one exact document digest and trace it through rendering, extraction, chunks, retrieval, context, and changed output.
carrier: Cinder document experiment trace bundle spanning extraction, retrieval, context, and decision.
participant_surface: LibreOffice/document tools, Cinder Jupyter, and independent document evaluator

title: Borrow A Trusted Voice
description: Create a new, credible audio message in the voice of a trusted Orion partner and preserve the exact media and provenance for later delivery.
hints: Use the verified public talk recording for the partner whose role fits the release-review context.
Clean, sufficiently long reference speech and a natural script matter more than repeated blind generation.
Review the audio yourself, meet the published intelligibility and similarity bounds, and export the exact WAV and manifest together.
carrier: Cinder media registry immutable provenance record.
participant_surface: Cinder Jupyter media environment, audio player, and media registry

title: Deploy A Disposable Relay
description: Build and deploy a Cinder-owned serverless relay on your domain and prove it survives a scale-to-zero cycle.
hints: Deploy from your attacker Forgejo repository through the normal Knative build path.
Preserve source, image, deployment revision, domain, and TLS continuity.
Invoke the service, wait for visible scale-to-zero, invoke it again, and inspect the deployment lifecycle record.
carrier: Knative lifecycle record spanning build, TLS, first request, scale-to-zero, and cold start.
participant_surface: Cinder Forgejo, Harbor, Knative, PowerDNS, TLS, and Kali terminal

title: Stage The Cinder Front
description: Assemble the exact Cinder infrastructure, model route, tools, and artifacts prepared in this act into one verified and signed staging front.
hints: Use the native digest or resource identifier produced by each earlier operation; do not rebuild artifacts.
Prove that model traffic crosses your LiteLLM route and that every staged object matches its local bytes.
Sign the complete manifest, verify it from Kali, and preserve the signed file for delivery and compromise operations.
carrier: Cinder Forgejo Actions staging artifact after provider, route, digest, ownership, and signature checks.
participant_surface: OpenRouter, Cinder LiteLLM, MinIO, Harbor, Forgejo Actions, and Cosign
